touches.claim: Revenue concentration in a small set of hit franchises—Grand Theft Auto generated 12.4% of fiscal 2026 net revenue and 12.6% of six-month fiscal 2027 net revenue, while leading franchises accounted for 54.3% of fiscal 2026 net revenue—creates acute exposure to release delays and post-launch disruptions.

Because a concentrated set of top franchises generated 54.3% of full-year net revenue, sustaining franchise-led growth requires retaining key creative talent, funding rising development budgets, and avoiding quality or launch disruptions.

news.headline: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ generates $3.79 billion, biggest entertainment launch ever
news.quote: Grand Theft Auto VI has generated $3.79 billion in revenue worldwide

touches.claim: Take-Two depends heavily on hit titles and Grand Theft Auto, which contributed 12.4% of fiscal 2026 net revenue and 12.6% of six-month fiscal 2027 net revenue while five best-selling franchises accounted for 54.3% of fiscal 2026 net revenue, making its $8,000 to $8,200 (table in millions) fiscal 2027 Net Bookings outlook vulnerable to delays or weak market acceptance of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI (scheduled for November 19, 2026) began in June 2026 with initial demand outpacing historical series benchmarks, underpinning reiterated fiscal 2027 Net Bookings guidance of $8.0 to $8.2 billion.

Revenue concentration in a small set of hit franchises—Grand Theft Auto generated 12.4% of fiscal 2026 net revenue and 12.6% of six-month fiscal 2027 net revenue, while leading franchises accounted for 54.3% of fiscal 2026 net revenue—creates acute exposure to release delays and post-launch disruptions.

Rockstar Games' planned release of Grand Theft Auto VI, supported by pre-orders outpacing historical series benchmarks, underpins Take-Two's full-year Net Bookings outlook of $8,000 to $8,200 (table in millions).

Hit-title growth requires timely game delivery without development delays, strong market acceptance, continued growth in PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S installed bases, and ongoing console platform approvals from Sony and Microsoft.

news.why: Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in worldwide launch sales with 32.5 million presold copies, delivering record market acceptance that substantially de-risks Take-Two's $8.0 to $8.2 billion fiscal 2027 Net Bookings outlook.

business_model.claim: Its portfolio spans internally owned and selectively licensed franchises—led by Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K, Borderlands, Red Dead Redemption, WWE 2K, and Zynga mobile titles such as Toon Blast, Match Factory!, Empires & Puzzles, and Color Block Jam—and includes Grand Theft Auto VI, which generated $3.79 billion in day one retail sales upon its November 19, 2026 release.
quotes: Most of our intellectual property is internally owned and developed, which we believe best positions us financially and competitively.

Our net revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 was led by a variety of our top franchises, primarily NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto, Borderlands, Red Dead Redemption, and WWE 2K, as well as our top mobile contributors, primarily Toon Blast, Match Factory!, Empires & Puzzles, and Color Block Jam.

NEW YORK, NY, November 20, 2026 – Rockstar Games®, a label of Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO), is proud to announce that Grand Theft Auto VI day one retail sales* reached $3.79 billion, setting a new record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes predominantly from mobile and console platforms via digital online distribution, with mobile at 50.1%, console at 39.0%, and PC and other at 10.9% of net revenue in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, while digital online channels provided 97.0% in that fiscal year and 97.9% in the six months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Net revenue from mobile increased by $391.0 and accounted for 50.1% of our total net revenue in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, as compared to 52.2% in the prior year period.
Net revenue from console games increased by $498.2 and accounted for 39.0% of our total net revenue in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, as compared to 37.3% in the prior year period.
Net revenue from PC and other increased by $133.6 and accounted for 10.9% of our total net revenue in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, as compared to 10.5% in the prior year period.
Net revenue from digital online channels comprised 97.0% of our net revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.
Net revenue from digital online channels comprised 97.9% of our net revenue for the six months ended September 30, 2026.

business_model.claim: Take-Two sells globally to consumers—ranging from game enthusiasts to casual gamers—through digital storefronts, platform partners, large retail customers, third-party distributors, and its direct-to-consumer platform, and sells in-game advertising to marketers and advertisers, with 60% of net revenue in the United States and 40% International for the six months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: We sell software titles both digitally and physically through direct relationships with digital storefronts and platform partners, large retail customers, and third-party distributors.
We manage a direct-to-consumer platform, primarily for our mobile business, to drive purchases directly with our consumer base.
Our advertising offerings provide creative ways for marketers and advertisers to reach and engage with our players and are generally essential for our free-to-play titles.

business_model.claim: Customer and platform distribution is highly concentrated: the five largest customers accounted for 80.6% of net revenue in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026—with Apple, Sony, Google, and Microsoft each accounting for more than 10.0%—and Apple and Google platforms generated 91.0% of mobile revenue.
quotes: Sales to our five largest customers during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, accounted for 80.6% of our net revenue, with Apple, Sony, Google, and Microsoft each accounting for more than 10.0% of our net revenue.
In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, we derived 91.0% of our mobile revenue on Apple and Google platforms.

business_model.claim: On its Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations, Take-Two disaggregates net revenue into Game ($2,798.8, table in millions) and Advertising (232.1, table in millions) out of 3,030.9 (table in millions) in total net revenue for the six months ended September 30, 2026.

Revenue fluctuates significantly with the timing, seasonality, and commercial reception of hit titles, as the five best-selling franchises generated 54.3% of net revenue in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 and Grand Theft Auto alone contributed 12.4% in that year and 12.6% in the six months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Grand Theft Auto products contributed 12.4% of our net revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, and the five best-selling franchises (including Grand Theft Auto), which may change year over year, in the aggregate accounted for 54.3% of our net revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.
The life cycle of a console or PC title generally involves a relatively high level of sales during the first few months after introduction followed by a rapid decline in sales.
Sales of Grand Theft Auto products generated 12.6% of our net revenue for the six months ended September 30, 2026.

business_model.claim: External revenue drivers include third-party console installed base growth, hardware generation transitions, macroeconomic conditions and global tariff policies affecting consumer spending and hardware pricing, and foreign currency exchange rates.
quotes: The success of our business is dependent upon consumer acceptance of these platforms and the continued growth in the installed base of these platforms, which has been and could be impacted by global economic factors, including global tariff policies.

When new hardware platforms are introduced, demand for interactive entertainment developed for older platforms typically declines, which may negatively affect our business during the market transition to the new consoles.

We continue to monitor various macroeconomic and geopolitical factors, such as global tariff policies, that may affect our business in several areas, including consumer demand, inflation, pricing pressure on our products and third party hardware platforms, credit quality of our receivables, and foreign currency exchange rates.

quotes: Further, as a result of the platform fees associated with online game sales, our mobile net revenue generally generates a lower gross margin percentage than our Console or PC revenue.
The agreement requires us to submit products to Sony for approval and for us to make royalty payments to Sony based on the number of units manufactured or revenue from digitally downloaded content.
Additionally, Microsoft charges the Company fees and royalties under the Agreement for each physical media product manufactured on behalf of the Company.

competitive_position.claim: Take-Two faces intense competition from larger, better-resourced game publishers and technology companies—including Sony, Microsoft, Apple, Google, Tencent, Electronic Arts, Nintendo, Epic Games, Roblox, and Ubisoft—as well as alternative entertainment like social media, television, and movies.
quotes: We also compete with game publishers, such as Electronic Arts, Embracer Group, Epic Games, Microsoft, Nintendo, Playrix, Playtika, Roblox, Savvy Games, Sony, Tencent, and Ubisoft.

Some of our competitors have greater financial, technical, personnel, and other resources than we do and are able to finance larger budgets for development and marketing, make higher offers to licensors and developers for commercially desirable properties, adopt more aggressive pricing policies to develop more commercially successful video game products than we do, recruit our key creative and technical talent or otherwise disrupt our operations.

Our titles also compete with other forms of entertainment, such as social media, in addition to motion pictures, television, short-form video, and audio and video products featuring similar themes, online computer programs and other entertainment, which may be less expensive or provide other advantages to consumers.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the FY2026 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Low barriers to entry in mobile and online gaming, amplified by artificial intelligence tools, expose Take-Two to title proliferation, competitor imitation of hit games, and rising player acquisition and retention costs.
quotes: Additionally, competitors may develop content that imitates or competes with our best-selling games, including by using AI to do so, potentially reducing our sales or our ability to charge the same prices we have historically charged for our products.

We also compete or will compete with a vast number of small companies and individuals who are able to create and launch games and other content for devices and platforms using relatively limited resources, including AI resources, and with relatively limited start-up time or expertise.

Increasing competition could result in loss of players, increasing player acquisition and retention costs, and loss of talent, all of which could harm our business, financial condition or results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the FY2026 Form 10-K Items 1A and 7 and Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Console hardware transition cycles, supply chain or tariff-driven hardware price increases, and macroeconomic downturns threaten console demand and increase dual-generation development costs.
quotes: Historically, when next generation consoles are announced or introduced into the market, consumers have typically reduced their purchases of products for prior-generation consoles in anticipation of purchasing a next-generation console and products for that console.

During console transitions, we may simultaneously incur costs both in continuing to develop and market new titles for prior-generation video game platforms, which may not sell at premium prices, and also in developing products for next-generation platforms, which may not generate immediate or near-term revenues.

We also rely on the availability of an adequate supply of these video game consoles (which sometimes has been negatively affected by supply chain issues, and which has been and could be affected by an increase in tariffs or trade restrictions on component parts) and the continued support for these consoles by their manufacturers, including our ability to reach consumers via the online networks operated by these console manufacturers.
